newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Senate panel approves pension reform bill.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Senate panel approves pension reform bill.

text.p: A Brazilian Senate committee approved Thursday the government's pension reform bill, a congressional official said.
The committee voted 18-2 in favor of the bill which seeks to stem a growing deficit in Brazil's social security system, the official said.
The committee was due to vote next Tuesday on several amendments to the bill.

Once the amendments have been voted, the bill goes to the floor of the Senate where it needs two three-fifths majorities for approval. It must also return to the Chamber of Deputies for approval of changes made in the Senate.
The legislation has been stuck in Congress for more than two years amid stiff opposition from public sector lobbies. They stand to lose an array of perks and benefits as a result of the reform.

Government officials agreed earlier this week to a latest compromise over the text of the bill, watering down an article which would have ended the practice of raising public sector pensions to match pay hikes given to workers.
